passages.original: [1315] Prolicere, emanare, effluere. Varro : Demum ubi prolicuit dulcia unda.
passages.english: [1315] Prolicere: to flow forth, to stream out. Varro: "At last, when the sweet wave flowed forth."
passages.notes: Glossary entry. The lemma 'prolicere' (normally 'to entice forth') is glossed here as 'to flow out'; it is perhaps a confusion with 'proluere' or 'prolabi', or a corruption of the form. 'Dulcia unda' is ungrammatical as it stands (neuter plural adjective with a feminine singular noun). The text may be corrupt, e.g. for 'dulcis unda' or 'dulcia ... unda[s]'. The translation follows the sense 'sweet wave'.
